To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
higher donor renal volume, as measured by CT, is associated with higher renal function in living donor kidney transplant recipients, and this relationship is linear, with no threshold effect.

higher donor kidney volumes are associated with higher eGFRs in recipients at 12 months after live-donor kidney transplantation, and that using this criterion, transplant centers may potentially select better donors from among those with multiple potential donors.

higher donor kidney volumes are associated with higher eGFRs in recipients of living-donor transplants, and a volume threshold of 145 cc/m2 can help identify donors with a higher likelihood of providing a kidney with good graft function at 1 year post-transplantation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of renal volume on post-transplant graft function.
the relationship between living donor kidney volume and graft function at 1 year post transplantation.
the effect of donor renal volume and its estimation on recipient graft function at one year.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the volume of living donor kidney has no significant effect on graft function at the end of first year after transplantation.
a donor kidney volume of 145 cc per recipient BSA is associated with a higher likelihood of graft function above 50 ml/min at 12 month post transplant.
the higher the donor renal volume, the better the postoperative kidney function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the higher the kidney volume the better the graft function.

the donor renal volume is a strong predictor of graft function at 1 year, and a volume threshold of 145 cc per m2 of recipient BSA may be useful to predict graft function at 3 months post-transplantation.
a donor kidney volume threshold of 145 cc/m2 BSA should be avoided, and that the voxel counting technique is more accurate than ellipsoid formula in the estimation of kidney volume.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a higher volume does not necessarily imply a better graft function.
the ellipsoid formula should be used with caution and that the correction factor may vary among populations.
a simple formula can be used to estimate kidney volume, and that a threshold of 145 cc per m2 recipient BSA is associated with an increased odds of a GFI <50 ml/min/BSA 1.73 at 12 month.
